correctness.rationale: The exact joint tilted-binomial weights and decreasing adjacent ratios are elementary and are verified exhaustively at n<=6. Mode comparison uses u=W((n-1)p²)/p; uniform ratio expansions hold because u=o(n), u→∞ and p²u→0. Concentration follows geometric tails; three event-probability regimes follow a uniform upper bound, a critical Stirling/Laplace LDP, and concentration/small-second-moment arguments. Localization follows conditional edge independence and a union Chernoff bound. The checker ran 99 assertions; proof covers all n asymptotics.

value.rationale: Zero rooted triangles is a natural local random-graph rarity. Its two competing mechanisms (degree suppression versus neighbor-edge suppression) switch exactly at p of order n^-1/2, with a Lambert-W critical law and full critical large-deviation rate. Global degrees outside the root stay typical. The result gives a qualitative structural phase change with a quantitatively exact event cost, not just a computed expectation or routine table row.
